text:
maya: CI on main is red — session_replayer_test failed twice but different asserts, looks timing-related.
ci-bot: build 4821 failed: https://ci.redwood.internal/4821/job/serve-tests (flaky) :rotating_light:
sam: which assert? can you paste the failing log lines?
maya: here —
```
AssertionError: expected order [A,B,C] but got [A,C,B]
at runtime/tests/session_replayer_test.cpp:132
2023-07-11 14:02:11.345 INFO kv_cache: evicted key session-123
```
devon: hmm ordering swap between C and B, looks like a concurrent enqueue in SequenceReplayer. Could be nondet scheduling.
lee: did this start after the retry-window refactor? commit 9f3b2a4 pushed yesterday.
maya: yes PR #2817 touched SequenceReplayer::push() + retry window.
carol: tagging @devon for bisect? also we should try a CI rerun with higher debug verbosity to capture thread interleavings.
devon: I can try a git bisect locally but tests on my machine are stable. Anyone able to reproduce in docker with stress flags?
sam: @maya can you trigger a one-off rerun with TEST_SEED=12345 and THREAD_COUNT=8? we have a helper in ci-tasks.
maya: kicked rerun: https://ci.redwood.internal/4823/job/serve-tests?seed=12345 (cc @ci-bot)
ci-bot: rerun queued by maya.
lee: if seed reproduces, please capture a thread dump and the env vars. Try also ASAN=1 build to catch UB.
maya: rerun finished — failed again with same mismatch and the log shows two pushes near-simultaneous:
```
[14:02:11.340] thread-7 push seq=42
[14:02:11.341] thread-3 push seq=42
[14:02:11.342] SequenceReplayer::apply: reordered packets
```
devon: that log ordering indicates a race in the internal buffer acknowledgement. I suspect SequenceReplayer::commit() has a non-atomic read-modify-write.
carol: can you post the minimal repro command? I'll try on macos runner.
maya: command: `ci-run --job serve-tests --filter session_replayer_test --seed 12345 --threads 8`
sam: @devon if you want to bisect, start at 9f3b2a4..main and stop on first bad. I can spare a couple hours of CI credits.
devon: starting bisect now, will report back. if bisect points to retry-window patch we should add an atomic or mutex and a unit test that simulates simultaneous push.
lee: quick workaround: add an exponential backoff in SequenceReplayer::push to serialize same-seq pushes until we decide root cause? low confidence. :thinking_face:
carol: prefer to understand root cause instead of adding heuristics. but we can add a CI-only stress test that spins threads to increase surface area.
maya: agreed. I opened an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/issues/4321 with logs + failing CI link.
devon: bisect update: first bad commit 9f3b2a4 -> touches retry-window and subtle reorder. Drafting a small patch to use atomic compare_exchange for index updates.
sam: awesome. @devon can you post the patch as a PR draft so CI can validate?
devon: will push PR/2824 with tests that run the stress harness. ETA a few hrs.
lee: if PR passes CI stress we can backport to release branches. also add a comment explaining why atomic is necessary.
carol: thanks everyone. if anyone else sees similar flakes, add the `session_replayer_race` label to the issue. :memo:
maya: adding label now and assigning devon. :thumbsup:
